name: Louis van Gaal

spellsCounted.reason: Eredivisie 1993-94 to 1995-96, Champions League 1994-95, UEFA Cup 1991-92 (counted spell decided by the user)
La Liga 1997-98 and 1998-99 (counted spell decided by the user)

scopeNote: Ajax 1991-97 and Barcelona 1997-2000. Sources call the Ajax shape 3-4-3 (Ballverliebt: 3-4-3 with a midfield diamond, 3-1-3-3; La Grinta: 3-4-3, 3-1-4-2 out of possession, 3-3-4 at the end of the 1995 final; Planet Football and FourFourTwo: '4-3-3/3-4-3'). The popular label 'typical 4-3-3' is questioned by Ballverliebt. The system is positional (roles tied to the position, not the player), with man-marking defenders (Reiziger, F. de Boer) and a libero (Blind) per Ballverliebt and La Grinta. Barcelona tactical coverage is thin: only the 4-3-3 / 2-3-2-3 labels and the Rivaldo-on-the-left role are verified. Most Ajax tactical facts are from the 1994-95 season (the day of individual matches is not always given, so season YYYY/YY dates are used). Rivaldo's 2002 statements and the Valdes/Iniesta debuts belong to the excluded 2002-03 spell and are not used as evidence. Partial dates: sources describing general habits across the spell use a representative season (1994/95, or 1992/93 and 1997/98 for debuts and Barcelona), and statedView dates 2005, 1999-12 and 1995 are approximations flagged in the source field. spellsExcluded years are approximate because those spells are not counted.
openQuestions: Formation label disagreement: Ballverliebt (3-4-3 with diamond / 3-1-3-3), La Grinta (3-4-3, 3-1-4-2 defending, 3-3-4 late), Bleacher Report 2014 and Goal Italia ('4-3-3 at Ajax') and a Substack piece (4-2-3-1, not mined). Confirm whether Van Gaal's own 4-3-3 label refers to slots rather than the shape.

Marking: Ballverliebt and La Grinta describe man-marking by defenders and midfielders in specific matches (1995 final, Bayern 1994-95); no source states a zonal base. Cox (Zonal Marking) says Van Gaal's Ajax used a high line and pressing but was seen only in a search summary, not mined.
High line and pressing intensity were not verified in a mined page; only the pressing triggers (immediate counter-press, collective hounding) are.
No Barcelona-specific tactical analysis (pressing, build-up, set-pieces, line height) found in a readable tier A-B page; the Barcelona 1998-99 analysis requested remains a gap.
The 'coach is the architect' quote was not found; only 'philosophy more than a system' (FIFA.com, undated).
Kluivert clash: no dated in-period source found for a Van Gaal-Kluivert conflict; only Rivaldo (1999-00) and Stoichkov (1997-98) are verified.
Date of the Goal Italia/FIFA.com 'philosophy' interview not found (likely c.2005).
Spielverlagerung and Coaches' Voice returned no Van Gaal pages in the site: searches.

statedView.quote: Football is a team sport and members of the team are therefore dependent on each other. If certain players do not carry out their tasks properly on the pitch, then their colleagues will suffer. This means that every player has to carry out his basic tasks to the best of his ability and this requires a disciplined approach on the pitch.
statedView.source: Kormelink and Seeverens, The Coaching Philosophies of Louis van Gaal and the Ajax Coaches, as quoted by These Football Times (2015-01-15)

statedView.quote: Milan play as Ajax play. They want to win the game, but PSG hang back and are primarily interested in avoiding defeat.

La mia è una filosofia calcistica più che un sistema. Un sistema dipende dai giocatori che hai. Io invece ho usato il 4-3-3 con l’Ajax, il 2-3-2-3 con il Barcellona e posso utilizzare il 4-4-2 con l’AZ. Sono flessibile. La filosofia, però, rimane la stessa.
statedView.source: Goal.com Italia 2022-08-08, citing FIFA.com (approximate year, AZ era; exact date not found)

statedView.quote: Friends of the press, I’m leaving. Congratulations.
In six years at Ajax I won more than Barcelona had won in a hundred.

I always put Rivaldo on the left. He did that very well. The team adapted to Rivaldo. [...] I told him that he would no longer play in the first team and that he had been voted the best in the world thanks to his team-mates and because he was on [the left wing].
statedView.source: Goal.com 2024-05-31 (date approximated from the Ballon d'Or episode; the interview date was not found)

statedView.quote: Cruijff would later describe Van Gaal’s methods as a ‘militaristic way of working’ that prioritised computers and statistics over intuition and creativity. (Cruyff's view of Van Gaal, kept as the press contradiction to the system-first reading)
statedView.source: Holland Times 2025-07-08 (date of Cruyff remark not found; 1995 is an approximation)
